title: Bigfoot in NC: The legend, the sightings and ties to a WNC costume shop
excerpt: Bigfoot remains a persistent element of Western North Carolina folklore and tourism despite scientific skepticism and claims that the famous 1967 Patterson-Gimlin film featured a costume created by a ...
content:
HENDERSONVILLE, N.C. (QUEEN CITY NEWS) -- For generations, the mountains of western North Carolina have been home to stories of the unexplained. Few legends have proven quite as enduring, or elusive, as Bigfoot.

From reported sightings deep in the woods to merchandise sold in local shops, the mysterious creature has become a familiar part of mountain folklore.

"Some people are really Bigfoot enthusiasts because they are really searching for Bigfoot, and then some people just think it's funny," said Lisa Waldrop, a Hendersonville business owner.

But long before Bigfoot became a souvenir, stories of mysterious creatures roaming the mountains were passed down through generations.

Local folklorist Jason Tapp said the region's history has helped shape those stories.

"We have a rich history of mountain men themselves and lumberjacks where they were taking down trees out in the forest," Tapp said. "At the end of the day they would sit around a campfire and try to explain why they keep hearing footsteps around them."

Tapp said those experiences helped give rise to stories about creatures such as Bigfoot and the Wampus Cat.

"It's trying to explain the unexplainable, and next thing you know, you have a narrative," he said.

In 1967, a few seconds of grainy footage filmed in Northern California gave the world what many believed was its first real look at Bigfoot.

Known as the Patterson-Gimlin film, the footage shows a large, hairy figure walking through a wooded area.  Nearly 60 years later, its authenticity remains a subject of debate.

Sean Morris, owner of Morris Costumes, said his grandfather, Philip Morris, created the costume used in the famous footage.

"Back in 1967, my grandfather made the original costume for the famous black-and-white Roger Patterson Bigfoot film," Morris said.

According to Morris, his grandfather was also a magician who believed in keeping the secrets behind his illusions.

"He was also a magician too, which magicians would never reveal their secrets," Morris said.

The family's account, if true, would mean one of Bigfoot's most famous appearances was an elaborate illusion.  

"I think that he was just more excited that it had fooled so many people for so many years, and people till this day believe that is a real Bigfoot," Morris said. "And I'm not saying that Bigfoot is not real, but that specific Bigfoot is not."

Regardless of whether Bigfoot exists, the creature has become a recognizable part of western North Carolina's culture and tourism.

"You know, Bigfoot brings people to town and Bigfoot brings people to shop and look for Bigfoot stuff," Waldrop said. "People love him. What can you say, people love Bigfoot."

While there have been no scientifically confirmed sightings of Bigfoot in the United States, more than 100 sightings have been reported in North Carolina over the past 50 years. The majority of those have been in the western part of the state, according to the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization.

Scientists remain skeptical that an animal of Bigfoot's reported size could live undetected for so long.

Still, the reports continue, and so does the fascination.

"I think Bigfoot is like the mascot for everything strange and mysterious," Tapp said. "Once you flip that switch to acknowledging that we don't know everything that there is to know in the world, you have to accept that there could be a Bigfoot out there."

For all the places Bigfoot has appeared — on merchandise, in costumes and in famous footage — the search for evidence of the creature in the wild continues.
